_note: Driving Academy theory exam (design spec section 8.1). General road-safety knowledge for an in-game licence; not official guidance. Pass mark 80%. Graded on the server by /api/driving/theory.

questions.q: What is the usual speed limit on residential streets?
questions.why: Residential areas are usually 40 km/h because of children and pedestrians.

questions.q: Who must wear a seatbelt?
questions.why: Every person in the vehicle must be belted in.

questions.q: A child under 10 (or shorter than 145 cm) should sit…
questions.why: Young or small children must not sit in the front seat.

questions.q: Babies and toddlers up to 4 years old need…
questions.why: Small children must travel in a suitable child seat.

questions.q: You're entering a roundabout. Who has priority?
questions.why: Give way to vehicles already circulating.

questions.q: Using a hand-held phone while driving is…
options: An offence with a fine and black points
questions.why: Phone use while driving is fined and adds black points.

questions.q: What happens if you collect too many black points in 12 months?
questions.why: Reaching the black-point limit leads to suspension.

questions.q: Jumping a red light can lead to…
options: A heavy fine, black points and the car being impounded
Nothing if no one is hurt
questions.why: Red-light offences are among the most serious.

questions.q: An ambulance with sirens is behind you. You should…
options: Move aside safely and let it pass
questions.why: Make way for emergency vehicles as soon as it's safe.

questions.q: Overtaking using the hard shoulder is…
questions.why: The shoulder is for emergencies only.

questions.q: A pedestrian is waiting at a zebra crossing. You must…
options: Give way and let them cross
Speed past before they step out
questions.why: Pedestrians at a marked crossing have priority.

questions.q: Driving after drinking any alcohol is…
questions.why: There is zero tolerance for drink-driving.

questions.q: How do toll gates charge you?
options: Automatically through a tag on your car
You pay at the end of the year
questions.why: Tolls are charged automatically as you drive through.

questions.q: Following the car in front too closely (tailgating) is…
options: An offence; keep a safe gap
questions.why: Tailgating is fined; keep at least a 2–3 second gap.

questions.q: In fog or a sandstorm with poor visibility you should…
options: Drive faster to get out of it
Slow down, increase your gap and use dipped headlights
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving fast
questions.why: Slow down and stay visible; pull over safely if it's very bad.

questions.q: When do you use hazard lights?
options: When you've stopped because of a breakdown or danger
questions.why: Hazards warn others that you are stopped or there is danger ahead.

questions.q: You want to change lanes. What first?
options: Check mirrors and blind spot, then signal
questions.why: Mirror, signal, blind spot, then move.

questions.q: Which lane is generally for faster traffic on a multi-lane highway?
questions.why: Keep right unless overtaking; the left lane is for faster traffic.

questions.q: A yellow box junction means…
options: Don't enter unless your exit is clear
questions.why: Don't block a junction; enter only if you can clear it.

questions.q: You're tired on a long drive. The safest choice is…
options: Open the window and push on
Drink coffee and speed up to arrive sooner
questions.why: Fatigue is as dangerous as speeding; rest before driving on.

questions.q: Overtaking a school bus that has stopped with its stop sign out is…
options: Allowed if no children are visible
questions.why: Stop when a school bus shows its stop sign.

questions.q: Your car breaks down on the highway. First you should…
options: Move to the shoulder, switch on hazards and get everyone safely away from traffic
Leave it and walk on the road
questions.why: Get off the road, be visible, and wait somewhere safe.
